cards.title: Shrinking a number
cards.body: `n // 10` drops the last digit. Do it again and again, and the number shrinks until it reaches 0.
cards.code:
n = 345
while n > 0:
    print(n)
    n = n // 10

cards.title: Counting rounds
cards.body: Add 1 to a counter each time the loop runs to find out how many rounds it took.
cards.code:
n = 50
steps = 0
while n > 1:
    n = n // 2
    steps += 1
print(steps)

cards.title: Test the edge cases
cards.body: Always try the smallest input too. What does your loop do when the number is 0, and how many digits does 0 have?

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should add up the digits of 123 and print 6, but it never finishes. Which line is wrong?
cards.code:
n = int(input())
total = 0
while n > 0:
    total += n % 10
    n = n % 10
print(total)

bug.fix: `n % 10` keeps the last digit, so `n` never reaches 0. Line 5 should drop it instead: `n = n // 10`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.code:
n = 7
count = 0
while n > 0:
    n //= 10
    count += 1
print(count)
check.explanation: 7 // 10 is 0, so the loop runs exactly once.
